description: ERC-20 token identity (contract address, name, decimals) by ticker, from The Graph's hosted Subgraph MCP against Uniswap v3 on Ethereum mainnet. Every field it teaches is immutable — an address, a symbol, a name, a decimals count. A price or a TVL would change every block, and a fact that changes every block is retrieval, not memory. The subgraph is named here rather than searched for because the Subgraph MCP's own ranking signal (get_deployment_30day_query_counts) answered 0 for every candidate when this plan was written, and that server's instructions say to ask rather than guess when volumes cannot decide; naming it also spends one query per question instead of four. It takes ONE token per ticker, the most-traded one: the subgraph is permissionless, so a ticker is not an identity — asking for USDC on 2026-09-07 also returned an impostor at 0x9abc68b3 with an obscene name and a Wormhole-bridged USD Coin (PoS), both of which are true rows and neither of which anybody wants compiled into a model. Trading volume is the only signal this schema offers for telling the canonical token apart, so that is what is used, and it is a heuristic rather than a proof. The page size is not part of the shape, so this choice does not reset the lookup counter.

arguments.query: { _meta { block { number } } tokens(where: {symbol: "{symbol}"}, first: 1, orderBy: txCount, orderDirection: desc) { id symbol name decimals } }

mapping.prompt: What is the {chain} contract address of the {name} ({symbol}) token?

patterns: what is the contract address of {symbol}
what is the contract address of the {symbol} token
